newsitem.title: UK: AMEC profits surge 71 pct in year. [CORRECTED 11:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: AMEC profits surge 71 pct in year. [CORRECTED 11:50 GMT]

text.p: British construction and engineering group AMEC Plc on Thursday reported a 71 percent surge in annual pre-tax profits after exceptional items to 27.2 million pounds ($44.3 million). (Corrects figures and text to clarify that 71 percent increase in pretax profits was after exceptional items)

"It is pleasing to be able to announce pre-tax profits up 71 percent accompanied by further improvements in the group's cash position and a dividend increased by 33 percent. This level of increase demonstrates our confidence going forward," group chief executive Peter Mason said in a statement.

The group proposed a total dividend of 4.0 pence per share, up from 3.0 pence. Turnover climbed 13 percent to 2.77 billion pounds while net cash balances at the end of the financial year to December 31, 1996, stood at a five-year high of 63.4 million pounds, up from 14.5 million.

Mason said that in the 14 months since joining the company, the management structure had been reorganised, its housing subsidiary had been revitalised, 75 million pounds had been realised through disposals and it had transformed its international presence.
"My strategic review continues. We have made some positive progress, but I can see more that has to be done and in the coming months it will be done," he added.
The company announced that chairman Alan Cockshaw, who is to retire on July 14, 1997, will be succeeded as non-executive chairman by Sydney Gillibrand.
